problem.statement: A population has an unknown distribution of a value u (a planet's period and radius, a star's mass). A survey lists the objects it can see: each object has a selection probability that depends on its true value and on the target that was searched, and each listed object has a measured value x with its own known uncertainty sigma. The rates are the expected number of objects of the population per unit of exposure in each bin of the true value. One likelihood is committed; the planet occurrence engine of Prompt 229 is its special case with no per-object uncertainty.
problem.bins: J contiguous bins [e_0, e_1), ..., [e_(J-1), e_J] of the true value with widths w_j; the true value is uniform inside a bin (declared: no continuous model).
problem.exposure: E_j >= 0, the expected number of objects listed per unit rate in true bin j: the summed completeness of the searched targets for planets, the effective volume for stars. It is built from Prompt 154's selection object by E_j = sum over targets of weight_t times the mean of the target's inclusion probability over 64 midpoints of the bin (a target is {selection, weight}; for a volume the targets are shells of exact volume and the selection reads the shell's distance beside the value). It may also be given directly (the stored planet survey). Prompt 262's effective volume (the integral of the completeness over the volume) is the same quantity; its module is on a spike, not merged, so it is not imported, and leg A5 reproduces its hand case by this definition.
problem.reliability: r_j in (0, 1], the stated probability that a listing in bin j is real (default 1), never estimated here; false listings are taken to follow the distribution of the real ones of their bin (as in Prompt 229).
problem.rate: Gamma_j >= 0, the expected number of population objects per unit of exposure in true bin j (it may exceed one); mu_j = E_j Gamma_j / r_j is the expected number of listings that belong to true bin j.
problem.sample: either counts n_j (objects whose measured value is taken as exact: sigma = 0), or objects {x_i, sigma_i} with sigma_i >= 0 known and independent of the true bin (DEC2).
problem.likelihood: The listings are a Poisson process over the measured value. With K_ij = [Phi((x_i - e_(j-1)) / sigma_i) - Phi((x_i - e_j) / sigma_i)] / w_j (the density of x_i from a true value uniform in bin j: the convolution over bins; for sigma_i = 0, 1 / w_j if x_i is in bin j and 0 otherwise), the extended log-likelihood is  l(mu) = sum_i ln(sum_j mu_j K_ij) - sum_j mu_j  (terms that do not depend on mu dropped). Counts n_j with exact bins give l = sum_j (n_j ln mu_j - mu_j) and the maximum mu_j = n_j, so Gamma_j = n_j r_j / E_j: the rate of Prompt 229. l is concave in mu.
problem.maximum: mu_hat = the maximiser on mu >= 0 by the EM iteration (mu_j <- mu_j sum_i K_ij / D_i, D_i = sum_l mu_l K_il) accelerated by SQUAREM, started from a uniform mu summing to the number of objects; the counts path uses the closed form. Bins with E_j = 0 are not in the model.
problem.interval: The profile-likelihood interval of Gamma_j at level L: the set of Gamma with D_j(Gamma) = 2 [l(mu_hat) - max over the other mu of l with mu_j = E_j Gamma / r_j] <= chi-square quantile of L on one degree of freedom. D_j is convex (the partial maximum of a concave function), so the set is an interval; its ends come from bracketing and bisection on D_j. The upper end is null (status unbounded) when D_j has not reached the threshold at 1e6 times max(mu_hat_j, 1) r_j / E_j. The counts path returns Prompt 154's Poisson interval (Garwood below 100 listings, the deviance interval above) at exposure E_j / r_j, so that Prompt 229's intervals are reproduced exactly; its method string says so.
problem.zero: A bin whose maximum mu_hat_j is below 1e-6 is not given an interval: it gets the one-sided upper limit at 95 percent, the Gamma at which D_j equals -2 ln(1 - 0.95) (for a count of zero this is exactly -ln(0.05) / E_j, Prompt 229's limit).
problem.floor: A bin with E_j below 5 is not constrained: no rate, no limit (Prompt 229's floor); if every bin is below the floor the result is not constrained as a whole. The bin stays in the fit, so that its listings are not forced into its neighbours.
problem.resolution: The result states the median of sigma_i / w over the objects and `resolutionOk` = (that median is at most 0.5). The committed domain is resolutionOk: a bin narrower than twice the typical uncertainty is not resolved and the likelihood leaves the split between neighbours to the data's noise.
problem.penalty: A toggle, named as a penalty. With kappa > 0 the estimate maximises  l(mu) - (kappa / 2) sum_(j=2)^(J-1) (theta_(j-1) - 2 theta_j + theta_(j+1))^2  with theta_j = ln Gamma_j, over all bins (every bin needs E_j > 0). It is a roughness penalty on the log rate, a regularisation chosen by the user; it is not a prior and its result is not a posterior, and no interval is returned for a penalised estimate (the result carries the unpenalised fit beside it). kappa = 0 is the unpenalised maximum.
problem.limits: No continuous model of the distribution, no sampler (D-SAMPLER-01), no marginal likelihood, no hierarchical or population-of-populations model, no fitting of sigma, no model for the dependence of selection on sigma, and no more than 64 bins.

constants.note: Declared defaults, set before any measurement and not tuned to a result. levels are the one-sigma level of Prompt 229 and the usual 95 percent.

tolerance.note: oracleMu and oracleEndpoint are relative, for bins whose maximum mu_hat is at least 1 (endpoints: relative, or absolute 1e-6 where the oracle's end is 0). oracleLogLik is absolute. penaltyOracle is the largest absolute difference of ln Gamma. continuity compares the profile path at sigma = 1e-4 w to the counts path.

verdict.B: BASE PASSES and UNC does not: without per-object uncertainties (Part B builds the counts path on arbitrary bins and exposures, 229's engine on a general bin list and a general exposure, and nothing that takes a sigma).

amendments.recordedBefore: the oracle's first run and every validator run
amendments.text: Definitions the contract left open, fixed before any number existed. (1) The resolution record's width: w_i is the width of the bin that contains the measured value x_i (the nearest bin if x_i is outside the edges); the record is the median of sigma_i / w_i and resolutionOk = (median <= 0.5); sigma_i = 0 objects count as 0. (2) The reported statement of a bin in a coverage ensemble is covered when: status ok and D_j(Gamma_true) <= the chi-square threshold of the level (measured by one extra constrained fit at the truth); status upper-limit and Gamma_true <= the limit (at the 0.95 limit level, also in the 0.6827 ensembles); status not-constrained, refused or not converged: not covered. A bin with an unbounded upper end is covered by the same test. (3) The relative width of D1 is (hi - lo) / Gamma_hat over the bins with status ok and a finite hi; the median is over every such (replicate, rich bin) pair, and the ratio is of the medians. (4) C5's ratio uses the replicates that converged. (5) C6 counts every fit, the unconstrained fit and each constrained fit at the truth. (6) P3's sum runs over all ten bins, with the unpenalised fit as the kappa = 0 fit; a replicate in which either fit does not converge is dropped from both and counted. (7) The zero rule is tested on the fit: mu_hat_j < 1e-6 (listing units). (8) In the oracle's reference samples the bins' truth mu is the expected number of listings of the bin (not the rate) and counts are Poisson draws of it. No bound is moved.

Two departures from the letter of two legs, recorded before any validator run and moving no bound. (1) Hand example A2 (and the oracle's A2) has exposure 1 in each bin, which is below the floor of 5, so both are run with the floor option set to 0 so that the intervals exist; the floor itself is tested by D5 and D6. (2) Leg P1 is evaluated on S1, S3, S4, S5 and S7: S2 and S6 hold bins whose unpenalised maximum is zero, for which the log rate does not exist, so the comparison of a penalised log-rate with it is not defined there; this is a stated reduction of the leg's samples, not a pass. (3) The truth rates of scenario M are the oracle's pinned gamma (mu*_j divided by the oracle's quadrature exposure), and 'rich' is decided from the prototype's exposure times that gamma.

amendments.recordedBefore: the second and later validator runs; recorded AFTER the first run, which it describes
amendments.text: What the first validator run showed and what changed because of it. The first run (pinned as first-run-results.json, thresholds sha256 as of AM2) gave 41 pass, 2 fail (D8, P2), 6 reported, 3 not run, letter B. D8 is a failure of the leg as committed and stays failing (see the gate document). P2 is not: the validator computed P2's status with a condition that the committed bound does not contain (that every penalised fit meets the Newton gradient criterion), and R2, Q3, V1 and V2 carried the same kind of extra condition (convergence). The committed bounds are the numerical ones in the checks array; the validator is corrected so that every status is computed from the committed bound alone, and the convergence counts become measured fields. Under the committed bound P2 passes (the largest absolute difference of ln Gamma to the oracle is 9.1e-9 against 1e-4; 2 of the 6 penalised fits had stopped at the gradient criterion, 1e-10 absolute, in 1000 iterations). No other row's measured numbers change, no bound moves, no leg is added or removed, and nothing in the prototype changes. The oracle and the stream are run again against the file that carries AM3. This is a correction of the validator to the contract, made after a result, and is flagged to Carl as such.

decisions.text: The likelihood is stated from its definition, an extended Poisson-process likelihood over the measured value with the true value uniform in a bin, and checked against an independent implementation, not transcribed from a source: no text of any paper on deconvolution or occurrence calculations was available, so their printed forms are request R4 and the correspondence is NOT RUN. A verdict is therefore V-internal, synthetic and oracle.

Each object's sigma is known, Gaussian and independent of its true bin; it is not fitted and the selection is not made to depend on it. Where the selection depends on the measured value (a cut on x) the exposure is not the one of this likelihood; that case is outside the domain.
Reliability and false listings follow Prompt 229: a stated input per bin, false listings distributed like real ones of their bin.

Intervals come from the profile likelihood on the object path and from Prompt 154's Poisson interval on the counts path, so that Prompt 229's intervals are reproduced exactly; the method string names which, and continuity between them is leg Q3. Coverage of a profile interval is measured by the equivalent test D_j(Gamma_true) <= threshold, which is exact because D_j is convex.

The penalty is a roughness penalty on the second difference of the log rate: a quadratic form with one user-chosen weight kappa, named as a penalty everywhere, no interval returned for the penalised fit, never described as a prior, a posterior, a credible or a Bayesian quantity.

The exposure generalises Prompt 229's summed completeness and Prompt 262's effective volume into one quantity built from 154's selection object. No second selection-function object is built and Prompt 262's unmerged module is not imported (its truncation estimator, which failed a leg, is not relied on in any way here; the censoring estimator is not needed).

The maximum is found by EM with SQUAREM acceleration: the log-likelihood is concave in mu, so a fixed point of the EM map is the global maximum; a fit that does not converge is reported, not accepted.

The scope of the letter is the pair of sets named in verdict: BASE (the general likelihood's counts case, its equivalence to Prompt 229, its exposure, floor and refusals) and UNC (everything that takes a per-object sigma). The penalty is a separate toggle with its own admission. A gate may not expand its tested scope by calling untested work another instance of the same family, so no mass-function claim, no initial mass function and no real sample rests on this gate.
